Prepare teaching materials from reviewed examples

Source: vignettes/ddl-materials.Rmd
ddl-materials.Rmd

A teacher may want to choose clear, contrasting examples, ask learners to explain patterns, and reuse the activity in another class. This guide prepares a learner handout and a separate teacher record from explicitly reviewed source occurrences. Learners need a browser or a printed handout, not R. An R user prepares the search and runs the input/output steps; a teacher can edit the selection and activity tables.

Use development ldfreq 0.5.0.9001; see the installation instructions. ddl_material() and ddl_material_write() are installed examples to source explicitly, not exported functions. Construction revalidates the existing phrase review and requires optional quanteda >= 4.5.0. Japanese input also requires a UTF-8 LC_CTYPE locale; the bilingual demo runs in that environment. Reopening a completed material record and writing it again uses only ldfreq’s required packages.

Run the authored English and Japanese examples 

demo <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
sys.source(system.file("examples", "ddl-materials-demo.R",
  package = "ldfreq", mustWork = TRUE), demo)
helper <- demo$helper
x <- demo$materials$en # Use $ja for the Japanese handout.
x$selected[c("phrase_id", "pre", "keyword", "post", "citation")]
#>   phrase_id             pre  keyword        post                       citation
#> 1 departure         Please  take off  your coat. ldfreq authored example: en s2
#> 2 departure The plane will  take off       soon. ldfreq authored example: en s1
x$candidate_summary
#>       status count
#> 1   accepted     5
#> 2   rejected     0
#> 3 unresolved     2
#> 4 unreviewed     3

The English examples contrast uses of take off. The Japanese examples contrast contextual interpretations of ashi o hippatta. They are authored, MIT-licensed illustrations with manually specified token boundaries, not observations from a textbook corpus or an evaluation of an automatic analyzer. The new teaching-selection criterion is separate from the earlier phrase-sense review. Both clear interpretations can be selected for comparison.

Each handout contains two selected examples. Other accepted, unresolved and unreviewed candidates remain in the private record. Selecting examples does not imply that the complete candidate collection has been reviewed.

output <- tempfile("ldfreq-teaching-")
files <- helper$ddl_material_write(x, output)
stopifnot(identical(readRDS(files["record"]), x))
basename(files)
#> [1] "learner.html" "teacher.csv"  "material.rds"

For actual teaching, replace the temporary directory with a lasting new directory inside an existing parent, for example "materials/lesson-01". An existing directory or file is rejected; the writer never overwrites it. Open learner.html in a browser and print using the paper size you need. Check the print preview at the intended size, especially for long contexts or citations. Browser fonts and pagination can differ.

File Audience and contents
learner.html Selected original KWIC contexts, bold matched expressions, teacher-written prompts, response space, citations and usage notices. Self-contained UTF-8 HTML with print styling; no scripts or external assets.
teacher.csv The same selected occurrences in display order, original segment text, IDs, source coordinates, decisions, prompts and teacher notes. UTF-8; import fields as literal text.
material.rds Complete private record: original search and text, all decisions including pending ones, selection, activities, source declarations, settings and session. Keep it for reuse; do not distribute it as the learner handout.

Teacher notes, decision reasons, unselected rows and complete source records are not embedded in the learner file, including hidden elements. The selected KWIC still includes its original surrounding text: inspect that context before distribution. A selected context can contain another expression that is also matched elsewhere in the review.

Prepare your own reviewed candidates

Start with the phrase-review workflow. It accepts complete source-aligned annotations and an explicitly declared phrase list. Its existing search matches at least two tokens, exactly and case-sensitively, by their original surface forms. A word such as influence alone is outside this first recipe; an explicitly tokenized sequence can be searched. Japanese inflections and spelling variants are not automatically merged. Keep the analyzer, dictionary, token unit and original text in the annotation record; see Japanese annotations.

Use a criterion such as “clear contrasting contexts for this observation task”. An example rejected for this activity is not thereby incorrect language. The following continues from before, a phrase_list_review() result:

write.csv(before$worksheet, "decisions.csv", row.names = FALSE,
  na = "<MISSING>", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
# In the table, edit only status, reviewer and reason; keep every original row.
decisions <- read.csv("decisions.csv", colClasses = "character",
  check.names = FALSE, na.strings = "<MISSING>", encoding = "UTF-8")
review <- helper$phrase_list_review(before$source, before$criterion, decisions)

Use accepted, rejected, unresolved or unreviewed as documented in that workflow. Only accepted IDs can be selected for a handout. You need not finish reviewing every candidate, but pending candidates remain pending in the saved record. A no-match target remains in the review’s count table. A handout needs at least one selected example; no matches or no accepted examples produce an input error rather than an empty worksheet presented as a completed lesson.

Supply the teaching tables 

x$activities
#>   activity_id
#> 1     observe
#>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              prompt
#> 1 1. Compare the uses of the highlighted expression.\n2. Group the examples and underline the context supporting each interpretation.\n3. Explain your proposed distinction and check another example.\n4. Write your own example and explain the intended meaning.
#>                                                          teacher_note
#> 1 Teacher only: contrast a flight's departure with removing clothing.
x$items
#>                                                      occurrence_id activity_id
#> 1 5a93271e18c09f51f0859db14bc67e7a6d3ba6b9f2aa0a002425bb321c6d6aa2     observe
#> 2 c18d34d6f3910132a5b0cf972b1c88658b0e0cc2de243c7f263ee57fefafc19d     observe
x$sources
#>   document_id segment_id                       citation
#> 1          en         s1 ldfreq authored example: en s1
#> 2          en         s2 ldfreq authored example: en s2
#>                                                            usage
#> 1 MIT. Authored teaching examples; not observed corpus evidence.
#> 2 MIT. Authored teaching examples; not observed corpus evidence.
Table Required columns and interpretation
activities Unique activity_id, learner-facing prompt, private teacher_note (use "" if empty). Rows set activity order.
items Unique accepted occurrence_id and its activity_id. Row order sets example order within each activity. Every activity must have an example; accepted examples not listed here are not distributed.
sources document_id, segment_id, learner-facing citation and usage. Supply exactly one row for each selected source pair, with nonblank attribution and usage text.

IDs and text columns must be character vectors without missing values. These tables can be stored as UTF-8 CSV and read with colClasses = "character". The activity prompt can contain several numbered questions separated by newlines. Teacher notes can describe the intended contrast, alternative interpretations or discussion points; they are not automatically correct answers. The source usage text is a declaration supplied by the teacher, not an automated license check or permission grant.

rebuilt <- helper$ddl_material(
  review = x$review,
  activities = x$activities,
  items = x$items,
  sources = x$sources,
  title = x$title,
  language = "en" # "ja" changes the fixed handout labels.
)
stopifnot(identical(rebuilt$selected, x$selected))

Every input string is treated as literal text, not HTML or Markdown. Emphasis is applied only to the original matched span. No source text is rewritten, normalized or silently shortened. Formula-like character fields in the teacher CSV receive an apostrophe prefix for display; the unmodified values remain in the RDS. This CSV is an output reference, not the editable review worksheet.

Different phrase IDs at the same or nested source spans remain different candidates. Choose which ones to distribute; the recipe does not silently deduplicate them or convert their selected proportions into corpus frequencies. The material fingerprint detects accidental changes; it does not establish that annotation, attribution, permissions or pedagogical judgments are correct.

Design the observation task

The authored prompts ask learners to compare contexts, group interpretations, explain their evidence, check another example, and produce their own use. The teacher supplies the further example and decides how to discuss competing explanations. Neither highlighting an expression nor deleting a word by itself establishes an effective data-driven learning activity.

Use the textbook progression guide to inspect where target expressions recur and choose revision opportunities. That concordance record and the phrase-review record have different input formats and IDs; they are not interchangeable. A general corpus, a local textbook and a selected classroom worksheet also represent different collections. Retain their source and selection boundaries instead of treating the handout as a representative frequency sample.

This recipe does not download corpora, parse textbook PDFs, infer teaching level, generate readings or furigana, choose examples by a quality score, collect learner responses or grade them. Such information, when needed, must come from an explicit source or teacher judgment.

Reopen and reproduce without a new search 

library(ldfreq)
helper <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
sys.source(system.file("examples", "ddl-materials.R",
  package = "ldfreq", mustWork = TRUE), helper)
saved <- readRDS("materials/lesson-01/material.rds")
helper$ddl_material_write(saved, "materials/lesson-01-copy")

This uses the stored examples and original session record without loading quanteda or searching again. To change the selection or prompts, rebuild with ddl_material() from the saved review and revised teaching tables. Do not edit the sealed record or its fingerprint to bypass the source checks.
